body:
**Description**
When compiling with `-HV 202x -T ps_6_7 -E PSMain` it works and produces DXIL, when adding `-spirv` it SIGSEGVs the compiler.

**Steps to Reproduce**
https://godbolt.org/z/WasWzsq4E

If you strip all my C++ compat code then you have
https://godbolt.org/z/dWMfjxza1

**Actual Behavior**
SIGSEGV of the compiler.

I think this is because `static` outside of the class makes no sense in C++ (and for LLVM), but I cannot use `const` on its own because I get a different problem.

**Environment**
- DXC version Latest trunk according to Godbolt
- Host Operating System Linux I guess

comments.body: Thanks for reporting. Assigning to @cassiebeckley to take a look.

Huh, interesting. Thanks for pointing that out, I'll update the backend then.

Btw it works for non-array types
https://godbolt.org/z/9G7vnhesr
and on this simple repro
https://godbolt.org/z/ze8jaoM3z

But this is a full explicit specialization out of line initialization, not a partial.

Now the original thing has a useful error
```
error: casting to type 'void' unimplemented
```
https://godbolt.org/z/14badfxqE

Btw I don't get one thing, in c++20 for out of line `consexpr`  declarations, I'd use `const static` at the member declaration.
```cpp
template <typename float_t>
struct GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>
{
    const static float_t wi[2];
};
```
and then for the out-of line definitition `constexpr` or `constexpr inline` depending on the linkage I want
```cpp
template<typename float_t> constexpr inline float_t GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
```
https://godbolt.org/z/sr9vh3Gbb

For obvious reasons  in HLSL I need to use just `const` for the OOL definition.
```cpp
template<typename float_t> const float_t GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
```
With C++ it actually results in the same codegen if I don't do any exporting or linking
https://godbolt.org/z/W3cnYjqb1

Our repro was always wrong
```cpp
template<typename float_t> const static float_t GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
```
and compiler should emit a diagnostic like C++ https://godbolt.org/z/M9hajz5eE
```
<source>:13:34: error: 'static' can only be specified inside the class definition
   13 | template<typename float_t> const static float_t GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
      |                                  ^~~~~~
1 error generated.
Compiler returned: 1
```
instead I get
```
error: casting to type 'void' unimplemented
```

But then if I try to use the "correct" thing, we have https://godbolt.org/z/fExjP8rEM
```
<source>:14:28: error: 'const' is not a valid modifier for a field
template<typename float_t> const float_t GaussLegendreValues<2,float_t>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
```

So the error is that we don't get a diagnostic of trying to use `static` on a class/struct member outside the class definition, and that we get an error and a diagnostic when attempting to do the "right thing" (TM).

@sudonatalie I see that @cassiebeckley has left Google, is there chance anyone else gets assigned to this?

Changed the title to reflect that it also affects DXIL 
https://godbolt.org/z/6fnGf8f6q

It also doesn't fork on full specializations
https://godbolt.org/z/8TzvPPE3Y

It will give the same diagnostic even if you don't add `cosnt` (which you should) and misform the template
https://godbolt.org/z/xredxYY3x

And on a correctly formed full explicit specialization
https://godbolt.org/z/3e3veWxsc

funnily enough if you remove the `const` (to make it malformed) it gives diagnostics that make sense
https://godbolt.org/z/6f3h4a99c
```
<source>:15:37: error: redeclaration of 'wi' with a different type: 'float [2]' vs 'const float [2]'
float GaussLegendreValues<2,float>::wi[2] = {1.0, 1.0};
                                    ^
<source>:15:37: note: previous declaration is here
```

All happens without `-spirv` as well.

The fun part is that as soon as we remove the templating, we get expected behaviour

`const` without `static` in OOL initialization
https://godbolt.org/z/WvdKs7KnM

However its a bit disappointing that `const static` on the OOL is accepted
https://godbolt.org/z/hW1z876cW
@Keenuts I don't get why the issue is closed if all the repros I gave still fail ?
They do? In this case we can re-open.

> They do? In this case we can re-open.

first thing is that DXC wants me to use `static const` at the OOL definition site, when it should be just `const`
https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/5823#issuecomment-3637214466

second is that I can't OOL define members of a templated struct, even with explicit instantiation

title: Out-of-line initialization of `static const` member arrays doesn't work, and wrongly requires `static const` at definition site
